workflows.title: connect / session / version

observations: doctor: connected=true, versionMatch=true, resultChannel=true, bridgeVersion=4.1.78.34f5b8d9, exit 0.
--help first line is 'JLCEDA Pro 4.1.78.34f5b8d9'; commands: activate/open/stop/doctor/session/invoke/functions/doc + --mcp.
open --headless returns a sessionId in about 1 s, but the project keeps loading afterwards: polling getCurrentProjectInfo() needed ~3.9 s.
getReadyState() still returned 'notLoaded' after getCurrentProjectInfo() already returned the full project tree, so it cannot be used as a load gate.
There was exactly one origin=user session before and after the run; this spike only drove origin=cli sessions opened by itself.

risks: ok:true/exit 0 only means the call ran, not that the business state is correct
a CLI-opened window leaks unless session close --destroy is used

waitForDocumentReady() returned false for both the page uuid and the tab handle even though the page was activated and components were readable; it is not a usable readiness gate.

sch_Net.getAllNets(), getAllNetsName() and getCurrentProjectAllNets() all returned [] on a loaded project whose Protel netlist is 34,413 bytes, so the typed net API cannot be the source of truth; parsing the netlist text is required.
Component read required allSchematicPages=true to see the whole design; per-page reads follow the active document.
risks: net enumeration API returns empty on this fixture/version - silent data loss if trusted
background/inactive pages return shallow data; explicit page activation is required
text objects and title-block content were not probed in this run

observations: A catalog has 15 schematic read actions (including connectivity and nets) but the acceptance matrix marks every real-host row BLOCKED at M1; later self-evidence claims M2 PASS.
A's net/pin read is a typed action with declared readback semantics, which would remove the netlist-parsing step - but we have no independent A receipt.
blockers: not run by this spike (no Go build; connector only in the user's window)
A self-evidence is not our measurement and cannot upgrade this cell beyond static

workflows.notes: Official read works; the net API gap is closed by parsing the Protel netlist, which the Skill already does offline (netlist_diff.py).

workflows.title: schematic write + readback

observations: The typed write surface exists in the static API catalog (create/modify/delete/netflag/netport, wire create, save) with documented async conventions.
No write was executed: design-content write probes were not authorized for this session, so no receipt can support a covered/partial status.

Known 4.1.78 frictions from the repository's own adapter notes (eda-execution.md) still apply: new primitives commit asynchronously, property edits can be dropped, and ok:true does not mean the business operation succeeded.
risks: hand-written JS per operation, no typed contract, no idempotency guarantees
async commit timing requires waits + readback; a naive model call will report false success
no write probe means persistence is unproven

observations: A catalog has 26 schematic write actions and its self-evidence claims a real schematic write/save/reopen chain (M2-M4).
A typed action removes the JS-authoring and readback-batching burden; this is the strongest non-replaceable argument for A.
blockers: not run by this spike (no Go build, connector in user window only)

workflows.notes: This is the decisive unmeasured cell: official coverage cannot be established without an authorized write probe on a disposable temp project.

observations: Static surface: importChanges, PCB primitive modify/delete, PCB_Document.save and an official autoRouting entry point exist.
No write was executed (no authorization); the repository's own notes say importChanges returned true but materialized nothing in half-offline mode.
risks: importChanges may silently no-op in half-offline mode
single-writer / ordering / undo semantics are absent at the CLI layer
no write probe means persistence is unproven

observations: A catalog has 58 PCB write actions plus typed route/pour/drc helpers and claims a real M4 board build (layout, autoroute 6/6, pours, DRC 0).
A's typed write actions are a real cost advantage over hand-written JS for PCB.

workflows.title: batch / plan application

commands: 1 x lceda-pro invoke with a 10-read JS batch
observations: Measured CLI round-trip cost: 10 separate invokes took 10,082.7 ms (about 1,008 ms each); one invoke doing the same 10 reads took 995.6 ms.
Batching inside one JS program is about 10x cheaper than one invoke per action, so the model should compose a plan per invoke instead of calling one invoke per object.
There is no typed batch/transaction semantics: each invoke is an independent program; on timeout the CLI reports REQUEST_TIMEOUT and says the code may still be running and its result is discarded.
Write batching could not be measured (no authorization).
risks: timeout leaves unknown state; blind retry can duplicate creates
no per-action journal/idempotency key at the CLI layer
long JS programs are opaque to review and hard to resume

observations: A's daemon keeps a task log with request ids and states, which is a real advantage for resumable batches; the CLI has nothing comparable.
Not run by this spike.

workflows.notes: A thin batch plan (compose one JS program + readback + journal written by the caller) can reproduce most of this; the CLI's 1 s round-trip makes per-call-per-action designs unacceptable.

workflows.title: check / DRC / DFM

observations: Schematic DRC with includeVerboseError=true returned a structured warning array (rule ATTRMATCHCODE, primitive ids) even though the documented return type is boolean; the receipt is usable as evidence.
PCB DRC returned a structured error-group tree (count 1: netlist mismatch because schematic changes were never imported on this sample) and realtime status false.
DRC acts on the active document: calling schematic DRC while a PCB document was active threw 'SCH_DrcUtil: doctype(3) not support check sch drc'.
No DFM-equivalent audit was found in the official surface (PCB_Drc has rules/check only); A's pcb check is a rebuild-based DFM audit.
risks: documented return type disagrees with the observed shape
active-document dependency; wrong doctype errors are easy to hit
DFM/process checks are out of scope for official DRC

observations: A self-evidence claims native schematic DRC PASS (0 violations) and PCB DRC 0 violations plus a DFM audit with 0 errors / 4 warnings on its M4 board.
A's check actions return typed receipts with counts and scope, which formats better than the raw official arrays.

workflows.notes: Official DRC is usable once the active-document rule is encoded; DFM remains an offline (Skill) or typed (A) capability.

workflows.title: export

observations: Real artifacts produced: Protel netlist 38,568 B sha256 7bb9874d..., BOM CSV 1,957 B, PNG 712,074 B (PNG magic), Gerber zip 1,292,203 B (zip magic), pick-and-place CSV 8,433 B.
Gerber and CPL are available through the official API (PCB_ManufactureData.getGerberFile / getPickAndPlaceFile); A's capability matrix lists gerber/drill/cpl as unsupported.

File objects cannot be written to disk with the independent-script permission: eda.sys_FileSystem.* throws until external-interaction permission is enabled. The workaround used here is to read the File in JS, base64 it through the invoke result and write the bytes from Python (PNG 712 KB relayed fine).
The CLI appends the requested extension even when the name already has one ('a2spike.net.net', 'a2spike-bom.csv.csv', 'a2spike-page.png.png').
risks: binary relay through JSON/base64 is awkward for large files and has no path/sha contract
file naming quirk breaks naive automation
Gerber layer/object selection defaults must be reviewed before production use

observations: A catalog: 3 export actions only; capabilities reports gerber.export/drill.export/cpl.export = unsupported (0 actions).
A self-evidence itself records Gerber/drill/CPL as gui_only and not claimed.
A project.export (native archive) is a capability the official CLI lacks at the same level, but it is not part of W08's manufacturing exports.

workflows.notes: Official route is strictly better than A for manufacturing exports: A has no Gerber/drill/CPL action at all.

workflows.title: save / reopen / stale

observations: Close/reopen works: the reopened session returned the same project uuid, same board/schematic/PCB uuids and the same tree.
Fixture hash was unchanged before/after the whole probe (1 file, sha256 824f6dcc...), proving the read/export probes did not mutate the project.
Save persistence is NOT RUN (authorization); without it a save -> reopen -> readback chain cannot be claimed.
risks: saved:true may still need reopen to prove persistence
stale-read detection is caller-side only at the CLI layer (no staleRisk field seen)
.eprj2 -> .eprj3 conversion on save could change file layout; unmeasured

observations: A defines six-state evidence (command_completed / readback_verified / save_confirmed / reopen_confirmed / electrical_passed / quality_passed) and claims save/reopen PASS on its own board.
A documents saved:true != persisted explicitly; the official route needs the same discipline encoded by us.

workflows.notes: Reopen is proven; persistence is not. This is the second decisive unmeasured cell.

workflows.title: error / permission / boundary

observations: Stable envelope {ok:false,error:{code,message}} plus a mirrored stderr line; codes observed: SESSION_NOT_FOUND (exit 3), INVALID_ARGS (1), DOC_QUERY_FAILED (1), EXECUTION_ERROR (1), REQUEST_TIMEOUT (3).
REQUEST_TIMEOUT message explicitly says the code may still be running in the render and its result will be discarded - callers must read back, never blind-retry.
Permission gate observed: eda.sys_FileSystem.* throws '未启用扩展和独立脚本的外部交互权限！' for independent-script invokes; this blocks direct file writes/reads outside the editor.
activateDocument(<bogus id>) returns false instead of throwing, so confusing 'silent false' with 'success' is possible.
risks: exit code alone is not enough; error.code must be parsed
silent-boolean APIs (activateDocument/waitForDocumentReady) need explicit checks
timeout leaves unknown side effects

actions: stable error codes NO_CONNECTOR / STALE_WINDOW / AMBIGUOUS_* / PRECONDITION_REFUSED / ACTION_ABANDONED / REQUEST_TIMEOUT-equivalent
observations: A protocol defines stable error classes and states that ACTION_ABANDONED may still land later, which is the same hazard the official REQUEST_TIMEOUT has.
Not run by this spike.

workflows.notes: Error envelope is good enough to build a typed gate on top; the caller must map codes, not exit codes.

workflows.title: MCP entry

observations: The official MCP server works over stdio with newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0; initialize returned protocolVersion 2025-06-18, serverInfo JLCEDA Pro 4.1.78.34f5b8d9, capabilities {tools:{}}.
tools/list exposes exactly 3 meta-tools: lceda-pro.help, lceda-pro.discover, lceda-pro.call (a proxy over the CLI command surface).
tools/call lceda-pro.help returned the same command tree as the CLI; no parameterless read tool exists other than help, so a real read call needs discover -> call with arguments.
HTTP transport (--mcp http --port 3030 --token ...) was not exercised in this run.
risks: 3 generic meta-tools mean the model must discover command paths itself
no typed MCP tools per action, no schemas per EDA operation
MCP calls still need a session/project context; concurrency/auth for HTTP mode is untested here

observations: A ships a CLI + daemon + WebSocket connector; it does not expose an MCP server, so B1 cannot use A as an MCP backend without writing a gateway.
The repository already has an unrelated offline-audit MCP server (docs/zhigou-mcp) that never touches EDA.

workflows.notes: For B1 Phase 2, the official MCP server is the only existing MCP entry; its three meta-tools are thin but real.
